thm-qftx-cw-fundamental-group-presentati:
## Statement

Let $K$ be a finite connected CW complex, let $v_0$ be a vertex, and let $T$ be a maximal tree in its 1-skeleton. Choose one orientation of each 1-cell outside $T$. For each such edge $e:u\to v$, let $x_e$ be the based loop that follows $T$ from $v_0$ to $u$, traverses $e$, and returns along $T$ from $v$ to $v_0$. For every 2-cell $f$, choose a point on its attaching circle and a path in the 1-skeleton from $v_0$ to its image; the resulting based attaching loop has a unique reduced word $r_f$ in the free basis $(x_e)$. Then

$$\pi_1(K,v_0)\cong \langle x_e\ (e\notin T)\mid r_f\ (f\text{ a 2-cell})\rangle.$$

Cells of dimension at least three add no generators or relators. Changing the connecting path conjugates its relator, and reversing an edge orientation inverts the corresponding generator, so these choices do not change the presented group.
def-gr-fx-thin-paths:
## Definition

Let $M$ be a smooth manifold and $U\subseteq M$ open. A **piecewise-smooth path** in $U$ is a continuous map $\gamma:[0,1]\to U$ for which some finite partition $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_n=1$ makes every restriction $\gamma|_{[t_{j-1},t_j]}$ smooth as a map of manifolds with boundary. Its source and target are $\gamma(0)$ and $\gamma(1)$. The collection of all such paths is a set: it is a subset, defined by separation, of the function set from $[0,1]$ to $U$.

Two paths $\gamma_0,\gamma_1$ with the same source $x$ and target $y$ are **thin-homotopic**, written $\gamma_0\sim_{\mathrm{thin}}\gamma_1$, if there is a continuous map $H:[0,1]^2\to U$ and a finite subdivision of the square into compact curvilinear triangles such that $H$ is smooth up to each triangle's boundary, $H(0,t)=\gamma_0(t)$, $H(1,t)=\gamma_1(t)$, $H(s,0)=x$, $H(s,1)=y$, and $\operatorname{rank}(dH_{(s,t)})\le 1$ on every smooth triangle. A **curvilinear triangle** here is a compact region equipped with a smooth parametrization from the standard closed two-simplex, smooth up to its three edges. The rank is the dimension of the image of the differential from the two-dimensional tangent space of the triangle to $T_{H(s,t)}M$. The quotient by this relation is used only after its equivalence and compatibility properties are proved.
prop-gr-fx-thin-path-quotient-groupoid:
## Statement

For every smooth manifold $M$ and open $U\subseteq M$, thin homotopy is an equivalence relation on each set of piecewise-smooth paths with fixed endpoints, and concatenation respects the equivalence classes. Tag a morphism by its endpoints and its path class. With objects the points of $U$, morphisms $x\to y$ the tagged classes $[\gamma]$ from $x$ to $y$, composition $[\delta]\circ[\gamma]=[\delta*\gamma]$ (first traverse $\gamma$, then $\delta$), identity the class of the constant path, and inverse $[\gamma]^{-1}=[\bar\gamma]$ where $\bar\gamma(t)=\gamma(1-t)$, the resulting category is a groupoid.
def-gr-fx-thin-path-groupoid:
## Definition

A **groupoid** is a category in which every morphism has a two-sided inverse. For an open subset $U$ of a smooth manifold, the **thin path groupoid** $\Pi^{\mathrm{thin}}_1(U)$ is the category whose objects are the points of $U$ and whose morphisms from $x$ to $y$ are tagged triples $(x,y,[\gamma])$, where $[\gamma]$ is a thin-homotopy class of piecewise-smooth paths from $x$ to $y$; composition, identities, and inverses are those of Proposition [[prop-gr-fx-thin-path-quotient-groupoid]].
prop-gr-fx-s1-loop-noncontractible:
## Statement

Let $S^1=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^2:x^2+y^2=1\}$ with its regular-level-set smooth structure. For $\gamma(t)=(\cos(2\pi t),\sin(2\pi t))$, $0\le t\le1$, the morphism $[\gamma]$ in $\Pi^{\mathrm{thin}}_1(S^1)$ is not the identity morphism at $(1,0)$.
prop-gr-fx-connection-path-transport-exi:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$ and let $0=t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_m=1$ be a finite partition. For each $j$, let $A_j:[t_{j-1},t_j]\to M_n(\mathbb R)$ be continuous. There is a unique continuous function $U:[0,1]\to M_n(\mathbb R)$ that is $C^1$ on each partition interval, satisfies $U'(t)=-A_j(t)U(t)$ in its interior, and has $U(0)=I_n$. Derivatives at interval endpoints are the corresponding one-sided derivatives.
def-gr-fx-connection-path-transport:
## Definition

Let $M$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold, $U\subseteq M$ a nonempty open set with a smooth tetrad, and $\omega$ its Lorentz-connection matrix from [[def-gr-fx-tetrad-spin-connection]]. Assume the supplier's $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention. For a piecewise-smooth path $\gamma:[0,1]\to U$, let $A_\gamma(t)=\omega_{\gamma(t)}(\dot\gamma(t))$ on each smooth piece. By Proposition [[prop-gr-fx-connection-path-transport-exists]], there is a unique continuous piecewise-$C^1$ solution

$$\dot U_\gamma(t)=-A_\gamma(t)U_\gamma(t),\qquad U_\gamma(0)=I_4.$$

The endpoint matrix $U_\gamma(1)$ is the **connection path transport** in the chosen tetrad trivialization. It maps vector components at $\gamma(0)$ to components at $\gamma(1)$ under the convention of the supplier. A smooth local Lorentz frame change transforms this matrix by its endpoint frame matrices; it is a gauge transformation in the principal-bundle sense only if it extends to an automorphism over the identity as in [[def-gauge-group-of-a-smooth-principal-bundle]].
prop-gr-fx-thin-transport-invariance:
## Statement

Under the assumptions of [[def-gr-fx-connection-path-transport]], if two piecewise-smooth paths $\gamma_0,\gamma_1:[0,1]\to U$ are thin-homotopic in the sense of [[def-gr-fx-thin-paths]], then $U_{\gamma_0}(1)=U_{\gamma_1}(1)$ in the fixed tetrad trivialization.
prop-gr-fx-path-functor-and-gauge:
## Statement

For transport as in [[def-gr-fx-connection-path-transport]], with composition convention $[\delta]\circ[\gamma]=[\delta*\gamma]$ meaning first traverse $\gamma$ and then $\delta$,

$$U_{\delta*\gamma}(1)=U_\delta(1)U_\gamma(1),\qquad U_{\bar\gamma}(1)=U_\gamma(1)^{-1}.$$

Let the target category have the tangent spaces $T_xM$ for $x\in U$ as objects, all linear isomorphisms between them as morphisms, and ordinary composition. Transport therefore defines a functor from the thin path groupoid [[def-gr-fx-thin-path-groupoid]] to this groupoid of tetrad fibers and invertible linear maps. Under the supplier convention $e'=\Lambda e$, the transport in the changed local frame satisfies

$$U'_{\gamma}(1)=\Lambda(\gamma(1))U_\gamma(1)\Lambda(\gamma(0))^{-1}.$$
prop-gr-fx-small-loop-curvature:
## Statement

Let $V\subseteq\mathbb R^n$ be an open coordinate domain, let $K\subset V$ be compact with positive distance from $\mathbb R^n\setminus V$, and let $\omega=\sum_k\omega_k(x)\,dx^k$ be a $C^2$ matrix-valued connection one-form on $V$. For $p\in K$, distinct coordinate directions $i,j$, and sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$ so the square stays in $V$, traverse the positively oriented boundary $p\to p+\varepsilon e_i\to p+\varepsilon e_i+\varepsilon e_j\to p+\varepsilon e_j\to p$. With the transport convention of [[def-gr-fx-connection-path-transport]],

$$U_{\partial R_\varepsilon}=I-\varepsilon^2F_{ij}(p)+O(\varepsilon^3),\qquad F_{ij}=\partial_i\omega_j-\partial_j\omega_i+[\omega_i,\omega_j].$$

Here the matrix norm is any fixed submultiplicative norm, and $O(\varepsilon^3)$ means its norm is at most $C\varepsilon^3$ for all sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$, with $C$ uniform for basepoints $p\in K$.
prop-gr-fx-su2-compact:
## Statement

Let $M_2(\mathbb C)$ have its Euclidean topology as $\mathbb R^8$, and define

$$SU(2)=\{Q\in M_2(\mathbb C):Q^\dagger Q=I_2,\ \det Q=1\}.$$

Under matrix multiplication, $SU(2)$ is a compact Hausdorff topological group.
def-gr-fx-discrete-holonomy-model:
## Definition

A **finite oriented graph** consists of finite vertex and edge sets $V,E$, source and target maps $s,t:E\to V$, and a fixed-point-free involution $e\mapsto\bar e$ with $s(\bar e)=t(e)$ and $t(\bar e)=s(e)$. A **finite SU(2) graph configuration** assigns $g_e\in SU(2)$ to every oriented edge and requires $g_{\bar e}=g_e^{-1}$. A graph path is a finite composable edge word $e_1,\ldots,e_n$; its holonomy is the later-left product $g_{e_n}\cdots g_{e_1}$, and the empty path has holonomy $I_2$.

A vertex gauge assignment is a function $h:V\to SU(2)$. It acts on edge variables by

$$g_e\longmapsto g'_e=h_{t(e)}g_eh_{s(e)}^{-1}.$$

A **finite-dimensional unitary representation** is a continuous group homomorphism $\rho:SU(2)\to U(W)$ for a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space $W$, where

$$U(W):=\{T\in\operatorname{GL}(W):\langle Tv,Tw\rangle=\langle v,w\rangle\text{ for all }v,w\in W\}.$$

For a closed graph path $\ell=(e_1,\ldots,e_n)$, the associated **Wilson trace** is

$$\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(\rho(g_{e_n})\cdots\rho(g_{e_1})\bigr).$$
prop-gr-fx-discrete-wilson-trace:
## Statement

For every finite SU(2) graph configuration, continuous finite-dimensional unitary representation $\rho$, closed graph path $\ell$, and vertex gauge assignment $h$, the Wilson trace of $\ell$ is unchanged by $g_e\mapsto h_{t(e)}g_eh_{s(e)}^{-1}$.
prop-gr-fx-vertex-haar-projection:
## Statement

Assume the full Axiom of Choice. Let a finite oriented graph be given, fix total orders on its finite vertex and edge sets, and for each edge $e$ choose a finite-dimensional continuous unitary representation $\rho_e:SU(2)\to U(V_e)$. At a vertex $v$ set

$$W_v=\bigotimes_{t(e)=v}V_e\;\otimes\!\bigotimes_{s(e)=v}V_e^*,$$

where the edge order induces the order on each factor list and an empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$. Use the dual action $g\cdot\lambda=\lambda\circ\rho_e(g^{-1})$ on $V_e^*$, with the dual Hilbert inner product determined by any orthonormal basis of $V_e$. On elementary tensors use the tensor-product inner product $\langle\bigotimes_i u_i,\bigotimes_i w_i\rangle=\prod_i\langle u_i,w_i\rangle$, extended sesquilinearly. Let $R_v$ be the resulting diagonal unitary representation. For the normalized Haar probability measure $\mu$ on $SU(2)$,

$$P_vw:=\int_{SU(2)}R_v(g)w\,d\mu(g)$$

is the orthogonal projection of $W_v$ onto its invariant subspace $W_v^{SU(2)}$. The vector integral is defined coordinatewise in the finite-dimensional space, equivalently by the weak integral in [[def-haar-averaging-operator-on-hom-spaces]]. On the coefficient space $W=\bigotimes_{v\in V}W_v$, with vertex order fixed as above, the operators $P_v$ acting on their respective vertex factors commute, and $\prod_{v\in V}P_v$ projects onto the tensors invariant at every vertex. This is a finite kinematic projection; it imposes no Hamiltonian or continuum constraint.
ex-gr-fx14-1:
## Statement

Let $M=S^1\times\mathbb R^3$, write $(x,y)$ for the standard embedding coordinates on $S^1$, and set $\alpha=x\,dy-y\,dx$. With real coordinates $t,z_1,z_2$ on $\mathbb R^3$, define

$$g=-dt\otimes dt+\alpha\otimes\alpha+dz_1\otimes dz_1+dz_2\otimes dz_2.$$

The global frame $E_0=\partial_t$, $E_1=-y\partial_x+x\partial_y$, $E_2=\partial_{z_1}$, $E_3=\partial_{z_2}$ is an orthonormal tetrad for $g$ with signature $(-,+,+,+)$. Orient $M$ by this ordered frame and time-orient it by $E_0$. Let $J$ be the constant matrix with $JE_2=E_3$, $JE_3=-E_2$, and $JE_0=JE_1=0$. Assume the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ convention in [[def-gr-fx-tetrad-spin-connection]]. Define $\omega=\tfrac14J\alpha$ and the affine connection on this frame by

$$\nabla_X\Bigl(\sum_Jv^J E_J\Bigr):=\sum_I\Bigl(X(v^I)+\sum_J\omega^I{}_J(X)v^J\Bigr)E_I.$$

This is a flat Lorentz connection. On any coordinate arc of $S^1$ with angular coordinate $\theta$, transport between endpoints is $\exp(-\tfrac14J(\theta_1-\theta_0))$, independent of the chosen path inside that arc. Around the once-around loop it is $\exp(-\tfrac\pi2J)\ne I_4$, although the curvature is zero; the loop is not thin-contractible.
ex-gr-fx14-2:
## Statement

Take the oriented triangle $v_0\xrightarrow{e_1}v_1\xrightarrow{e_2}v_2\xrightarrow{e_3}v_0$, assign $g_{e_1}=g_{e_2}=g_{e_3}=I_2$, and use the defining representation $\rho:SU(2)\hookrightarrow U(2)$. Let $k=\operatorname{diag}(i,-i)\in SU(2)$ and take the vertex gauge assignment $h_{v_0}=k$, $h_{v_1}=h_{v_2}=I_2$. The first and third edge matrices change to $k^{-1}$ and $k$, respectively, while the loop product remains $I_2$ and its Wilson trace remains $2$.
ex-gr-fx14-3:
## Statement

At a vertex with two incoming edges carrying the defining representation of $SU(2)$ on $V=\mathbb C^2$, the vertex space is $W_v=V\otimes V$. For a basis $e_1,e_2$ of $V$, the nonzero antisymmetric tensor

$$\epsilon=e_1\otimes e_2-e_2\otimes e_1$$

is invariant under the diagonal action $g\otimes g$. Consequently the normalized Haar projection $P_v$ of [[prop-gr-fx-vertex-haar-projection]] fixes it: $P_v\epsilon=\epsilon$.
